title: Choose a useful AI task and set a budget
outcome: Choose a bounded task and calculate a request budget.
story: Amina spends time sorting customer messages. An AI classifier could suggest categories, but it must stay within a budget and let staff handle uncertain cases.

frames.explanation: Generated output can change the cost considerably. These are invented exercise rates, not provider prices.
Check the maximum planned cost before spending. Record actual usage afterward.

sections.title: A model predicts a response
paragraphs: A language model produces tokens based on its input and learned patterns. It can classify, draft, and explain, but a convincing response can still be wrong. Give it a task with a clear outcome that you can check.

For the shop, begin with suggesting order, refund, or other. Keep actual refunds and record changes under service rules and human approval. Compare this with a simple keyword baseline: AI should earn its extra complexity with measured improvement.

sections.title: Tokens are units of model input and output
paragraphs: A token is a piece used by the model’s text representation; it is not always one word or character. Instructions, conversation, and retrieved context contribute to input. The generated answer contributes to output. Use the chosen provider’s tokenizer or returned usage when accuracy matters.

The lab receives token counts directly. Its rates of 2 and 8 fictional units per token are deliberately invented. For a real project, read the current pricing for your configured model and record the date and units. Never treat this arithmetic as a current price quote.

sections.title: Plan and observe spending
paragraphs: Set an input limit, a maximum output, a request timeout, and an overall budget. Check estimated maximum cost before the request, then record actual usage and latency after it. A retry also uses budget.

Shorter context is not automatically better: removing the policy needed to answer can lower quality. Compare quality, latency, and cost on the same examples. Keep the key on the server and let an account owner set the real spend limit.

sections.title: Define uncertainty and escalation
paragraphs: A model’s stated confidence is not a calibrated probability unless you establish that with evaluation. Use confidence as one signal and measure failures against labelled data. Decide which errors need human review before building the automation.

The project records a deterministic baseline and a real-model experiment separately. Browser fixtures teach control logic without a paid call. They cannot prove the accuracy, latency, or cost of a real model.

words.meaning: A unit used to represent model input and output.
A simpler approach used for comparison.
Passing a case to a person when automation should stop.

explanation: Input and output counts are supplied, not guessed from word length.
Each count uses its own invented rate.
The sum is an estimate in the exercise’s stated units.

exercise.title: A request budget guard
exercise.brief: Use input, output, and limit as non-negative whole numbers. Calculate cost = input*2 + output*8 using fictional rates. Return {cost, allowed}. Equality with the limit is allowed. Reject invalid numbers with RangeError.

steps.title: Calculate a cost
steps.task: For this step return the numeric cost.
steps.hint: Multiply each count by its stated rate, then add.

steps.title: Validate the counts
steps.task: Reject negative or non-integer input and output with RangeError. Still return a number.
steps.solution: function budget(input,output){if(!Number.isInteger(input)||!Number.isInteger(output)||input<0||output<0)throw new RangeError("Invalid token counts");return input*2+output*8;}

steps.title: Enforce the limit
steps.task: Return {cost,allowed}; validate limit too. Update earlier outputs to the final contract.
steps.hint: Use cost <= limit and a dictionary-shaped object.

cases.label: Invalid budget
cases.why: The limit is part of the contract.

project.title: An AI task worth testing
project.brief: Write a classifier experiment brief and compare a deterministic baseline with real model results when you have a server-side key and account budget. Keep the two reports separate.
deliverables: A labelled message dataset and baseline.
An experiment report with usage, latency, and limits.

milestones.title: Define the task
actions: Choose three categories and a human fallback.

milestones.title: Run a bounded experiment
actions: Configure the model and key on the server.
Set output, timeout, and spending limits.
Record real outputs and usage or explicitly mark the experiment not run.

acceptance: Fixture and model evidence are separate.
Limits and an escalation path are documented.

tests.expected: Human review is an allowed outcome.
No real accuracy claim is made.

project.extension: Compare two prompt versions on a held-out set without repeatedly tuning to that set.
reflection: Why might a simple baseline be sufficient?
Which token counts did you observe rather than estimate?
Which mistake must always reach a person?
